[LNUL.8.9] **`??` evaluation order — lazy, uniform (no mode-split).** `x ?? d`
evaluates `d` **only when `x` is `null`** (lazy short-circuit), in **both**
`realtime` and non-RT. The mode must not change it: `d` can fault where `x` is
present (`x ?? y / z`), so eager evaluation would raise a fault the lazy form
never meets, and a mode-dependent choice would make the **same program behave
differently** under `realtime` than without it. Unlike the operands of `and` /
`or` ([LNUL.4.2]), `x` and `d` are not interchangeable, so this order is part of
the meaning. WCET is unaffected — the worst case (`x` null → evaluate `d`) has the same bound
as eager.

idris.name: lnul_5_3__coalesce
idris.note: d is passed unevaluated and evaluated only when x is null: the lazy order, with no mode to split on in the model.

idris.name: lnul_5_3__null_takes_the_default
idris.note: The one case in which d is evaluated: x null, for every d.

idris.name: lnul_8_9__default_not_looked_at
idris.note: The clause's x ?? y / z with x present and z zero, quantified: for every non-null x and every d, a faulting one included, the answer is x and the fault is never met.
